decision.rationale: This is the November 4 decision finalized retrospectively after both research runs and the completed Trader Room, not a claim to have decided before the freeze. Original common market evidence: commit 612666a21e621e6bb437802cb48ace011f181b7b, overnight-20261104/review-001, stated cutoff 05:35:22 ET. Later information is separately identified: Kevin explicitly authorized the CNBC election article updated November 4 at 17:11Z, received in our later conversation; its reported Treasury rally and roughly 8% oil decline are asynchronous context, not common executable marks. Divided-government fiscal restraint and Iran de-escalation remain conditional hypotheses. I would initiate the reduced CORRA exposure from flat on this reviewed evidence because domestic persistence appears weaker than the remaining priced hike path, but the delivered hike and energy risk argue against adding. Partial profit-taking was already completed on November 3. Reject ACP387's U/Z-only recommendation: it conflated halving DV01 with expression improvement and did not establish relative mispricing. Reject ACP389's flat recommendation: it excluded authorized election context, imposed unsupported portfolio constraints and used stress asymmetry without a probability case. Its SR3-pay and receive-mark sign errors are recorded in research; they are not inputs to canonical marks or P&L. The next common packet must test how much election repricing has already happened before any new risk. No independent market/news retrieval was used beyond Kevin's expressly authorized article.
decision.synthesis: HOLD the existing $250m four-leg CORRA receive; no add and no new trade. Keep CAD/NOK long as a conditional candidate for the next shared evidence set. Consider opportunities by their policy, energy, growth, risk and financing components; neither opposing behavior nor overlapping correlation is by itself a reason to exclude a trade.
